items.title: US loses measles elimination status, major setback for US public health – video
items.summary:
The US lost its measles elimination status, global health authorities have announced on Tuesday, an official recognition that the infectious disease is endemic in the US after being declared eliminated for 26 years. The announcement comes as the US endures the worst measles outbreak since 1991 under Donald Trump and his health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, with more than 5,400 cases and eight deaths reported in the US in 2026

  • US loses measles elimination status amid worst outbreak since 1991

items.t: US loses measles elimination status, major setback for US public health – video

items.title: Sleep paralysis: when you’re awake, but can’t move – or even breathe | Letters
items.summary:
Readers recount their terrifying experiences of sleep paralysis in response to an article by Amy Fleming

I experienced sleep paralysis and hypnagogic hallucinations from childhood and into adulthood, with the episodes only waning in my 30s (Touch of evil: the terrifying truth about sleep paralysis, 11 November). I never spoke about them to anyone.

I experienced hallucinations in the form of severe perspective distortion (oversized bed and rooms) and full hallucinations/dream states, auditory hallucinations (screaming and loud thumping) and, of course, paralysis. I didn’t know at what point I was asleep or if I had woken and could easily slip back into a hypnagogic state. I only became aware of this state as an adult, having been referred to a psychiatrist on an unrelated matter.

Continue reading...
items.t: Sleep paralysis: when you’re awake, but can’t move – or even breathe | Letters

items.title: U.S. and Mexico officially lose measles-elimination status
items.summary: The U.S. has lost its measles-free status, international health officials said Tuesday, as the highly contagious virus once relegated to medical textbooks has spread — largely among the unvaccinated — at the highest rate in more than 30 years.
items.t: U.S. and Mexico officially lose measles-elimination status

Infectious disease is now continually spreading after being eliminated for 26 years, with more than 5,400 US cases

The US lost its measles elimination status, global health authorities announced, an official recognition that the infectious disease is endemic in the US after being eliminated for 26 years.

The announcement comes as the US endures the worst measles outbreak since 1991, with more than 5,400 cases and eight deaths in 2026.

items.title: Menopause symptoms aren’t always taken seriously. These female lawmakers plan to change that
items.summary:
From Utah to Louisiana, US states are making menopause care more affordable and accessible for midlife women

Melissa Shusterman was desperate for help with her menopausal symptoms: body aches, lethargy and brain fog, which she described as feeling “not myself”. The Pennsylvania state representative saw a gynecologist, a physical therapist, a chiropractor and a urologist. One doctor gave her lubricant, even though she’d already explained to him that sex was not the problem. (“Have you seen my husband?” she quipped.)

“I am more than lubrication,” Shusterman said. “I am a dynamic, smart, hardworking woman who wants to continue to feel good, so I can join my contemporaries, get back to work, and change things.”

Continue reading...
items.t: Menopause symptoms aren’t always taken seriously. These female lawmakers plan to change that

items.title: Ozempic and Mounjaro may have a surprising effect on your brain
items.summary: Blockbuster weight loss drugs like Ozempic and Mounjaro may do more than help people shed pounds, with growing evidence suggesting they could also influence brain health. Although studies have linked GLP-1 medications to a lower risk of dementia, major trials found that semaglutide did not slow Alzheimer's disease. Scientists suspect these drugs may be more effective at preserving memory and thinking abilities in people with obesity or diabetes, especially before cognitive problems appear.
items.t: Ozempic and Mounjaro may have a surprising effect on your brain

items.title: I'm a human doctor with human intelligence. But I sure do like my AI notetaker
items.summary: Has your doctor asked whether they can use artificial intelligence to take notes during an exam? It's very popular, and here's how to think through the pros and the cons of the new technology.
items.t: I'm a human doctor with human intelligence. But I sure do like my AI notetaker

items.summary:
Thanksgiving is just around the corner, just as millions of Americans are expected to travel for the holidays. Another thing that's upon us? Cold and flu season. 

(Image credit: Thibaut Durand)
items.t: More people are getting the flu. Should you get a flu shot before you travel?

items.title: Expert behind NHS children’s gender services review says she cannot back conversion practices ban
items.summary:
Hilary Cass says draft bill is having ‘chilling effect’ on healthcare professionals and could pose a risk to parents

The expert behind a major review into children’s gender services has said she can no longer support proposed legislation to ban conversion practices related to sexual orientation and transgender identity.

Hilary Cass, a paediatrician who now sits in the House of Lords, initially indicated her support when the conversion practices bill was announced in the summer. However, she has now said the proposed ban is having a “chilling effect” on healthcare professionals and could pose a risk to parents.

Continue reading...
items.t: Expert behind NHS children’s gender services review says she cannot back conversion practices ban

items.title: Health organization to announce that the U.S. has lost its measles elimination status
items.summary: The Pan American Health Organization is expected to announce that measles is no longer eliminated in the U.S. Record cases, lower vaccination rates and uncontained outbreaks led to the resurgence.
items.t: Health organization to announce that the U.S. has lost its measles elimination status

items.title: Wine, beer, or spirits? Massive study reveals a surprising health divide
items.summary: A massive study of more than 340,000 adults found that moderate wine drinkers had a 21% lower risk of cardiovascular death, while even light consumption of beer, cider, or spirits was linked to increased risk. Although heavy drinking was harmful regardless of beverage type, the findings suggest that the relationship between alcohol and health may be more complicated than previously thought.
items.t: Wine, beer, or spirits? Massive study reveals a surprising health divide

items.title: Cannabis addiction linked to 57% higher odds of suicidal thoughts
items.summary: A massive study involving more than 415,000 Americans has uncovered a concerning connection between cannabis use disorder and suicidal thoughts. Researchers found that adults with the disorder had 57% higher odds of experiencing suicidal thoughts, with women and younger adults facing particularly elevated risks.
items.t: Cannabis addiction linked to 57% higher odds of suicidal thoughts

items.title: 'It's close to bulletproof,' doctor says of MMR vaccine as measles cases rise
items.summary: Global health authorities are expected to announce that the U.S. has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, a public health milestone it achieved 26 years ago. This past year, the number of cases in the U.S. doubled, making it the worst year in three decades. That was the focus of the latest episode of Horizons with William Brangham.
items.t: 'It's close to bulletproof' doctor says of MMR vaccine as measles cases rise

items.title: Ministers to end Palantir’s contract with NHS in England in 2029
items.summary:
DHSC to extend US tech firm’s contract for two more years to allow time to line up British companies to replace it

Ministers will end the NHS’s contract with the controversial tech firm Palantir – but not until 2029, to allow time to line up British companies to replace it.

The Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) has decided to extend Palantir’s contract to provide the federated data platform (FDP) – the software that links different healthcare providers – for two more years rather than exercise a break clause that would have let them axe it next spring.

Continue reading...
items.t: Ministers to end Palantir’s contract with NHS in England in 2029

items.title: Damaging the lifeline that Samaritans offers the public | Letters
items.summary:
Volunteers despair as the charity sets about closing local branches and restructuring

Samaritans old and new will, I’m sure, have been just as shocked as I was by your article (‘Is anyone up for a fight?’: The battle for the soul of Samaritans, 10 November). Many, though, will not be surprised. I was a volunteer for 26 years in three branches. The work was demanding and life-changing; the experience is so transformative that it gives every part of society people who are strong enough to bear others’ burdens and able to share their pain. We don’t stop being listeners when we stop being volunteers.

During my time, I found that the people at the top were detached from what went on at branch level. It is not news to me that they cannot understand how central to the work each local branch is and how important every human contact is to those who need to talk.

Continue reading...
items.t: Damaging the lifeline that Samaritans offers the public | Letters

items.title: Naming your feelings can be harder than you think. This simple tool can help
items.summary:
About 10% of people have significant trouble identifying their emotions – which makes it harder to know what to do about them

Naming emotions is a core skill that most people develop as children, and it might seem like second nature. But research indicates that it’s harder than you think – about 10% of the general population have significant difficulty identifying their own emotions.

That’s why a simple tool called the feelings wheel has gained popularity in therapists’ offices and classrooms over recent years.

Continue reading...
items.t: Naming your feelings can be harder than you think. This simple tool can help

items.title: Surge of US datacenters adds equivalent of Denmark’s annual emissions, study finds
items.summary:
‘Hyperscaler’ datacenters across country draw upon dirtier power sources to meet vast energy needs, research shows

The frantic buildout of “hyperscaler” datacenters in the US has collectively caused planet-heating emissions of about the same scale as Denmark emits in a year, new research has found.

In that period, 403 “hyperscalers” – the largest datacenters used primarily to handle the growth of artificial intelligence – emitted about 25.7m metric tons of carbon dioxide, according to the study.

Continue reading...
items.t: Surge of US datacenters adds equivalent of Denmark’s annual emissions, study finds

items.title: Vitamin B12 may hold the key to treating a rare genetic disorder
items.summary: Scientists discovered that vitamin B12 largely reversed developmental abnormalities in worms carrying a genetic mutation linked to Verheij syndrome, a rare disorder that causes growth problems and developmental delays. Similar metabolic changes were identified in human patients, raising the possibility that this common vitamin could inspire new treatments for rare genetic diseases.
items.t: Vitamin B12 may hold the key to treating a rare genetic disorder

items.title: Scientists discover that the heart doesn't age the way we thought
items.summary: Scientists have discovered that the heart ages unevenly, with surprising hotspots of inflammation and scarring concentrated in the valves and major blood vessels rather than the heart muscle. The findings challenge long-standing assumptions about cardiac aging and could help researchers develop new ways to protect the heart as we grow older.
items.t: Scientists discover that the heart doesn't age the way we thought

items.title: A hidden biological divide may help explain Alzheimer’s and chronic pain
items.summary: New research reveals that biological sex, genetics, and menopause may dramatically influence Alzheimer's risk, treatment responses, and chronic pain conditions such as fibromyalgia. Scientists also uncovered surprising differences in immune activity and gut-brain interactions, opening the door to more personalized treatments for neurological disorders.
items.t: A hidden biological divide may help explain Alzheimer’s and chronic pain

items.title: A 19-year study reveals a troubling link between napping and death
items.summary: A surprising new study suggests that when and how often older adults nap could reveal hidden warning signs about their health. Researchers followed 1,338 people for up to 19 years and discovered that longer, more frequent naps were linked to higher mortality, while morning nappers faced a 30% greater risk of death than afternoon nappers. Each additional hour of daytime sleep was associated with a 13% increase in mortality risk.
items.t: A 19-year study reveals a troubling link between napping and death

items.title: New wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery
items.summary: A revolutionary new wearable patch could help people get more restorative sleep without medication or surgery. Developed by University of Texas researchers, the device uses gentle ultrasound to stimulate deep brain regions, helping participants enter REM sleep 43 minutes faster and remain there 16 minutes longer on average. The technology also showed promising effects on stress regulation and brain circuits involved in emotion.
items.t: New wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery

items.title: Tell us: have you been misdiagnosed with a medical condition?
items.summary:
We are looking for people to share their stories of misdiagnosis, how they realised this had happened, and perhaps found another diagnosis

Last month the actor Christina Applegate revealed that she had been misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis. She announced that she had the condition in 2021, and has spoken candidly about her experiences of it, becoming a prominent advocate for people living with MS.

“I’m back at square one ... I don’t know what’s going on with me.” Applegate said on her podcast MeSsy, adding: “There’s a pretty damn high number of misdiagnoses with MS.”

Continue reading...
items.t: Tell us: have you been misdiagnosed with a medical condition?

items.title: Why sleep matters when it comes to weight gain and loss
items.summary: Sleep can have a powerful impact on weight. Research shows it can affect appetite. There is also a two-way relationship between sleep quality and diet.
items.t: Why sleep matters when it comes to weight gain and loss

items.title: UK blood services issue urgent appeal for donations as winter approaches
items.summary:
Supplies are low and reserves of certain types are half of what the UK needs, officials say

UK blood services have issued an urgent appeal for 150,000 donations to help the NHS cope with the increase in demand that occurs during the winter.

Supplies of blood have run particularly low, with reserves of certain blood types only half of what is considered necessary, officials say.

Continue reading...
items.t: UK blood services issue urgent appeal for donations as winter approaches

items.title: Ministers accused of ‘gambling with safety’ for not knowing cost of NHS maternity unit repairs
items.summary:
NHS chiefs said last year that 43% of maternity and neonatal units in England do not meet safety standards

Ministers have been accused of “gambling with the safety of mothers and babies” after admitting they do not know how much repairing decrepit maternity units would cost.

NHS chiefs said last year that shoddy infrastructure meant 43% of maternity and neonatal units in England did not meet basic safety standards. Infrastructure problems hampered the delivery of clinical care thousands of times every year, NHS England said.

Continue reading...
items.t: Ministers accused of ‘gambling with safety’ for not knowing cost of NHS maternity unit repairs

items.title: MIT scientists discover a surprising way to boost the brain’s nighttime cleaning system
items.summary: MIT scientists discovered that carefully timed bursts of gentle pink noise during sleep can strengthen the brain’s natural cleaning waves, which help flush away potentially harmful waste. The breakthrough could pave the way for new treatments aimed at improving sleep and memory while potentially reducing the buildup of proteins linked to Alzheimer’s disease.
items.t: MIT scientists discover a surprising way to boost the brain’s nighttime cleaning system

items.title: Women prosecuted for abortions hail ‘historic day’ after receiving pardon
items.summary:
Calls for government to issue formal apology to those investigated after ending pregnancies in England and Wales

Campaigners and women previously convicted of illegal abortions have hailed a “historic day” after the pardoning of every woman who has faced criminal investigation for ending a pregnancy during the last 150 years.

A vote in the House of Lords earlier this year introduced legislation to pardon women accused of terminating their own pregnancies outside the legal framework and expunge their criminal records, under section 242 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026, which takes effect on Monday.

Continue reading...
items.t: Women prosecuted for abortions hail ‘historic day’ after receiving pardon

items.title: Art psychotherapists are already regulated | Letters
items.summary:
Elizabeth Donnelly notes that art therapists occupy a different regulatory position from counsellors and psychotherapists

We welcome the discussion about public protection, professional accountability and the importance of appropriate regulation within counselling and psychotherapy (Letters, 5 November). However, we feel it is important to highlight a distinction that may be helpful to readers.

Art psychotherapists are already a statutorily regulated profession in the UK, regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC). The HCPC regulates 15 health and care professions, including arts therapists (art psychotherapists, art therapists, drama therapists, music therapists) and the titles art therapist and art psychotherapist are legally protected. Practitioners must meet HCPC registration requirements, standards of proficiency, conduct and ethics, and continuing professional development requirements.

Continue reading...
items.t: Art psychotherapists are already regulated | Letters

items.title: Vitamin C could help block cancer-linked chemicals in your stomach, study finds
items.summary: Scientists have discovered that vitamin C may help prevent potentially cancer-causing chemicals from forming in the stomach after eating foods containing nitrates and nitrites. A new mathematical model suggests that taking vitamin C after meals could reduce these harmful reactions, offering a possible new strategy for lowering cancer risk.
items.t: Vitamin C could help block cancer-linked chemicals in your stomach, study finds

items.title: A common osteoporosis drug blocked spinal damage in a surprising new study
items.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising genetic connection to spinal degeneration and found that an existing osteoporosis drug can prevent damaging mineral buildup in zebrafish spines. The discovery could pave the way for new treatments that slow or prevent a major cause of chronic back pain.
items.t: A common osteoporosis drug blocked spinal damage in a surprising new study

items.title: Gen X is in worse health than boomers – and I have a few theories as to why | Emma Beddington
items.summary:
People in my age group are experiencing poorer physical and mental health than their elders at the same stage. Is this down to UPFs and booze, or something more complicated?

I almost choked on my bird-food breakfast recently, reading that gen Xers are in worse health than boomers. Research by the UCL Centre for Longitudinal Studies, on approximately 8,000 participants aged about 50 from the 1970 British Cohort Study, found that my generation is experiencing “worse physical and mental health across adulthood than earlier-born generations”.

Come on! How? We have better health education and pharmaceuticals than any previous generation, we’ve been browbeaten into cultivating our microbiomes and hitting our step counts, harassed to stand up (sitting’s worse than smoking!), jump around (protect your bones!) and pop creatine (unsure). Yet we’re still unhealthier than our elders?

Continue reading...
items.t: Gen X is in worse health than boomers – and I have a few theories as to why | Emma Beddington

items.title: Cold and health alerts issued for Scotland and northern England as snow and ice expected
items.summary:
UKHSA warns of health impact on those vulnerable to cold and urges people to check in with neighbours

Cold weather warnings have been issued for parts of the UK, and alerts for the risk to health services are due to begin on Sunday evening.

The Met Office issued yellow weather warnings for ice for central and eastern Scotland from 6pm on Sunday evening until 10am on Monday. People should be vigilant as they travelled, due to the risk from slipping on footpaths in icy conditions, it added.

Continue reading...
items.t: Cold and health alerts issued for Scotland and northern England as snow and ice expected

items.title: Laws limiting coal miners' exposure to toxic dust are in danger of being rolled back
items.summary: Coal miners who are exposed to silica dust are at a higher risk of black lung disease. Despite decades of advocacy, new efforts to regulate the toxic dust are under threat.
items.t: Laws limiting coal miners' exposure to toxic dust are in danger of being rolled back

items.title: A simple supplement could help your immune system fight cancer and viral infections
items.summary: A surprising discovery from Rockefeller University suggests that a common amino acid could play a powerful role in protecting against cancer and viral infections. Scientists found that low arginine levels interfere with the immune system's ability to recognize dangerous cells, while increasing arginine intake reduced colon cancer tumors and improved viral infection outcomes in mice. Even more remarkably, giving mice arginine after they contracted influenza helped them recover.
items.t: A simple supplement could help your immune system fight cancer and viral infections

items.title: Trump administration planning to reimburse doctors treating vaccine ‘injury’
items.summary:
Experts warn that sweeping changes elevate health secretary RFK Jr’s anti-vaccine agenda and personal profit

The Trump administration is finalizing a rule to reimburse doctors who diagnose, treat and counsel patients with side effects from vaccines in what experts believe is an attempt to undermine trust in vaccines and to create an evidence base on their purported risks.

Robert F Kennedy Jr, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), also announced the creation of a vaccine “injury” research center at the National Institutes of Health and has sought to reshape the Vaccine Injury Compensation Program (VICP) – actions that point to Kennedy’s longtime activism against vaccination as well as the profits he and his network have made from vaccine lawsuits.

Continue reading...
items.t: Trump administration planning to reimburse doctors treating vaccine ‘injury’

items.title: A new generation of disability rights activists carry on Judy Heumann's legacy
items.summary:
Being Heumann , premiering November 13, 2026 on Apple TV.'/> The film Being Heumann tells the lesser-known story of the mother of the disability rights movement. A new generation of activists share how they "carry the torch" today.

items.t: A new generation of disability rights activists carry on Judy Heumann's legacy

items.title: Alzheimer’s may start shrinking two brain regions years before memory loss
items.summary: Johns Hopkins scientists have uncovered hidden warning signs of Alzheimer’s disease that may appear up to a decade before memory loss begins. Brain scans revealed that two regions involved in memory and emotion start shrinking before the hippocampus, the area doctors typically examine for signs of Alzheimer’s. These early changes are linked to abnormal tau protein buildup and could provide a powerful new way to identify people at risk.
items.t: Alzheimer’s may start shrinking two brain regions years before memory loss

items.title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
items.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods, potentially revealing thousands of people at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that doctors might otherwise miss.
items.t: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death

items.title: US has lost measles elimination status, global health authorities say
items.summary:
The U.S. has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, according to researchers with direct knowledge of the deliberations at the Pan American Health Organization.

(Image credit: Amy Maxmen)
items.t: US has lost measles elimination status, global health authorities say

items.title: The U.S. flu season is off to a very early start. It's hitting the South and West now
items.summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Friday posted its latest update, reporting that seven states were reporting high flu activity last week, up from two states the week before.
items.t: The U.S. flu season is off to a very early start. It's hitting the South and West now

items.title: U.S. gives states another 6 months before they have to remove people from Medicaid for not working
items.summary: The administration clarified that while states still have the option to take action at the beginning of the year, they won't have to kick anyone off or deny coverage for failure to meet the requirement until July 1.
items.t: U.S. gives states another 6 months before they have to remove people from Medicaid for not working

items.title: NHS England on track to miss key cancer treatment target by 10,000 patients
items.summary:
Exclusive: 2,850 more patients a month would need to be treated within 62 days to meet March 2027 goal, as experts warn of failure of leadership

Nearly 10,000 more cancer patients in England will not be treated on time because the government will fail to meet its targets, amid a failure of leadership, focus and resource, experts have warned.

The NHS set an interim target to treat 80% of cancer patients within 62 days of urgent referral or consultant upgrade by March 2027. But with little more than 100 days to go, the proportion of patients starting treatment on time in September was 70.7%, down from 71.9% in August, NHS figures show.

Continue reading...
items.t: NHS England on track to miss key cancer treatment target by 10,000 patients

items.title: Scientists find a simple daily routine linked to less pain and depression
items.summary: A simple change to your daily routine could make a surprising difference in how you feel, both physically and mentally. University of Missouri researchers found that older adults who followed consistent daily schedules reported less physical pain and fewer symptoms of depression, even when they struggled with insomnia. Keeping regular times for sleeping, eating, and other activities may help regulate the body's internal clock, which influences mood, sleep, and overall health.
items.t: Scientists find a simple daily routine linked to less pain and depression

items.title: A new fiber supplement could help millions suffering from irritable bowel syndrome
items.summary: Scientists have developed a promising new fiber supplement that improves gut health in people with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) without worsening bloating, pain, or other digestive symptoms. The specially designed blend also improved gut-related anxiety and produced surprisingly rapid changes in gut bacteria, potentially offering a new way to manage IBS.
items.t: A new fiber supplement could help millions suffering from irritable bowel syndrome

items.title: Stanford scientists discover hidden brain signals that predict Alzheimer’s years before symptoms
items.summary: Stanford researchers have discovered that hidden patterns of brain activity can predict Alzheimer’s risk years before memory problems appear, potentially offering an earlier warning than traditional biomarkers. The same patterns also reveal which brains are unusually resistant to aging, raising hopes for future treatments that could help protect memory.
items.t: Stanford scientists discover hidden brain signals that predict Alzheimer’s years before symptoms

items.title: Exercise after ACL surgery may protect knees from early osteoarthritis
items.summary: A new study suggests that the right kind of exercise could help protect young adults from early knee osteoarthritis following ACL surgery. Researchers found that a four-month supervised rehabilitation program improved pain, muscle strength, and quality of life without damaging knee cartilage. The findings challenge fears that exercise worsens injured knees and could transform how patients recover from ACL reconstruction.
items.t: Exercise after ACL surgery may protect knees from early osteoarthritis

items.title: The abortion doctor who leads with her faith: ‘God is forgiving’
items.summary:
Dr DeShawn Taylor runs Arizona’s only Black woman-owned abortion clinic amid rapid legal changes

When gynecologist and abortion provider Dr DeShawn Taylor has conversations with patients about the afterlife, they ask her if they will be condemned for their choices. To quell their concerns, she shares with them Bible verses about free will. “If God wants that vessel, that spirit to get here, God will choose another vessel. You get to say, ‘I’ll pass,’” Taylor said at her clinic one spring afternoon, her short curly hair matching the color of her maroon scrubs. “I think that makes people feel a lot better with that understanding.”

As the founder and CEO of Desert Star Institute for Family Planning in Phoenix, Arizona, Taylor heads the only Black woman-run abortion clinic in the state, which also boasts a staff of women of color. On a Tuesday in March, pop music wafted throughout the waiting room filled mostly with Black and brown women, some with their children in tow. Bilingual posters about abortion care taped to the wall reflected the diversity of the clinic’s staff and clientele. On 6 February, an Arizona judge struck down state laws requiring patients to receive an ultrasound and to wait at least a day before receiving an abortion. With abortions now more accessible, a steady stream of clients poured into the office the…
items.t: The abortion doctor who leads with her faith: ‘God is forgiving’

items.title: Health is wealth? Polymarket and Kalshi now host bets on measles and other US health crises
items.summary:
Experts warn of risks of platforms hosting bets tied to US public health – including vaccine mandates and drug trials

The sign was pasted on a construction fence next to an elementary school in the Brooklyn borough of New York City. “Vaccines,” it proclaimed in bold capital letters against a blue star-spangled background – appearing, at first glance, to be like any other public health message on the importance of getting vaccinated.

But at the bottom of the sign, in smaller letters, it read: “Will any state end vaccine markets?” It was accompanied by the logo for Polymarket, an online prediction market where users can log in to wager on the outcomes of nearly any event – including, now, public health.

Continue reading...
items.t: Health is wealth? Polymarket and Kalshi now host bets on measles and other US health crises

items.title: A new policy could help solve the U.S. organ shortage. Critics say it's unethical
items.summary:
New guidelines are supposed to protect organ donors in a retrieval procedure that keeps blood flowing through livers, kidneys, lungs and hearts. But bioethicists have troubling questions.

(Image credit: Olga Pankova)
items.t: An organ transplant controversy tests 'the dead donor rule'

items.title: Yale scientists reveal what really slows aging and what doesn't
items.summary: Yale researchers have discovered that certain prescription drugs, healthy diets, and exercise can measurably slow biological aging, while popular anti-aging supplements appear largely ineffective. Their analysis of 51 studies could transform how scientists evaluate anti-aging treatments, although whether these biological changes actually extend life remains uncertain.
items.t: Yale scientists reveal what really slows aging and what doesn't

items.title: What men need to know after a major update to prostate cancer guidelines
items.summary: Middle-aged men should undergo regular screening for prostate cancer, the American Cancer Society said Thursday in a major change to its guidelines.
items.t: What men need to know after a major update to prostate cancer guidelines

items.title: Democrats are weighing impeachment of RFK Jr. while courting his supporters
items.summary: When Democrats take over Congress in January, one of their many oversight targets will be Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., whose overhaul of longstanding vaccine guidance and cuts to medical research over the past two years have drawn fiery criticism. Some high-ranking lawmakers have suggested impeaching him.
items.t: Democrats are weighing impeachment of RFK Jr. while courting his supporters

items.title: How Sen. Chris Van Hollen plans to flex Democratic power on the foreign aid front
items.summary:
He's the ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Subcommittee that oversees health aid and he's just announced he's running for Majority Leader. He spoke to NPR about his foreign aid vision.

(Image credit: Nathan Posner/Anadolu)
items.t: How Sen. Chris Van Hollen plans to flex Democratic power on the foreign aid front

items.title: Scientists discover a hidden danger of viral infections that vaccines may prevent
items.summary: A new study reveals that viral infections may leave behind hidden damage to the immune system long after symptoms disappear. Researchers found that mice recovering from an acute infection experienced lasting changes to their spleens and weakened immune responses, potentially leaving them more vulnerable to future threats. Surprisingly, prior vaccination completely prevented these harmful changes in the mouse model.
items.t: Scientists discover a hidden danger of viral infections that vaccines may prevent

items.title: Study of 750,000 pregnancies reveals a surprising twist about Ozempic and Wegovy
items.summary: A study of more than 750,000 pregnancies found that early exposure to Ozempic, Wegovy, and similar drugs was not linked to increased pregnancy complications when used for weight loss, but was associated with a higher risk of premature birth when prescribed for diabetes. The surprising difference suggests that diabetes itself may be driving the risk, although researchers caution that the drugs' safety during pregnancy remains uncertain.
items.t: Study of 750,000 pregnancies reveals a surprising twist about Ozempic and Wegovy

items.title: Stopping statins after 70 may be safer than expected, but there's a catch
items.summary: A major study of nearly 1,900 older adults suggests that stopping statins after age 70 may be relatively safe in the short term for people who have never experienced a heart attack or stroke. However, a higher rate of serious cardiovascular events or death during longer follow-up raises questions about the risks of discontinuing these widely prescribed medications.
items.t: Stopping statins after 70 may be safer than expected, but there's a catch

items.title: Without this protein, damaged muscle fills with fat and scar tissue
items.summary: Researchers have uncovered a surprising hidden function of a protein that may hold the key to repairing damaged muscles and treating muscular dystrophy. Known for protecting chromosomes, TRF2 also helps muscle stem cells maintain their identity and regenerate injured tissue. When scientists removed the protein in mice, muscles struggled to repair themselves, and muscular dystrophy progressed dramatically faster.
items.t: Without this protein, damaged muscle fills with fat and scar tissue

items.title: What to know about dengue fever as Florida reports more than 500 cases this year
items.summary: As Florida navigates its largest dengue outbreak in more than 15 years, it might help to understand how this virus spreads and how to recognize symptoms and protect yourself.
items.t: What to know about dengue fever as Florida reports more than 500 cases this year

items.title: WATCH: Trump administration officials announce PTSD research funding for psychedelic drug ibogaine
items.summary: Federal officials on Thursday announced new funding to explore the medical potential of ibogaine, a controversial psychedelic drug championed by veterans, conservative lawmakers and podcasters aligned with President Donald Trump.
items.t: WATCH: Trump administration officials announce PTSD research funding for psychedelic drug ibogaine
